payload.old_text: CORE RULE (all families, T=256-2048 steps; every task here is under-trained): rank choices by cumulative per-parameter displacement Δ. Adam/AdamW/RMSprop: Δ≈lr·T. Adagrad (zero-init accumulator, steps decay ~lr/√t): Δ≈2·lr·√T. SGD: Δ≈lr·T·|g|/(1−m) with raw grad |g|≈0.01 (bigram LM 0.003, MSE regression with momentum 0.03 — K1019), i.e. plain SGD ≈ Adam at lr/100, SGD m=0.9 ≈ Adam at lr/10. The largest-Δ choice wins 85% of optimizer-only and ~85% of mixed questions (after the lr-ceiling exceptions); a 1.5-3× Δ edge usually beats any architecture advantage. Use architecture rules only to break Δ ties (same optimizer+lr) or in architecture-only questions.
payload.text: For shared-model/data/budget optimizer comparisons BELOW task-specific saturation, use cumulative displacement Δ as a progress proxy, not a universal test-loss ranking. Check K1004/K1071-K1073 before choosing maximum Δ. Adam/AdamW/RMSprop: Δ≈lr·T; Adagrad: 2·lr·√T; SGD: lr·T·|g|/(1-m), |g|≈0.01 (bigram 0.003; momentum MSE 0.03, K1019). Older backtests favored larger Δ in ~85% after ceiling exceptions, but not every 256-2048-step task is under-trained. Across different architectures or optimizers, close Δ estimates are not decisive (K1012); use scoped architecture rules. Long-budget spiral/XOR maxima can lose (q_fb4a7f/q_46d72e); no validated general ceiling yet.

old.mechanism: SGD's step is the raw gradient, so its true displacement scales with the backpropagated gradient magnitude. With PyTorch default init (weight std≈1/√(3·fan_in)) each unnormalized block shrinks activations and hence hidden-layer gradients geometrically, so |g|≈0.01 overestimates Δ for deep plain stacks. LayerNorm restores unit-RMS activations per block, and Adam-family divide by √v, so both are insensitive. Predicts: collapse grows with depth, absent with ≥1 LN or adaptive optimizers.

new.mechanism: Unnormalized deep stacks can attenuate hidden activations and raw SGD gradients under default initialization; LayerNorm or adaptive scaling may reduce this problem. This is a candidate explanation for weak nominal-displacement credit, not a measured universal gradient bound. Pooled pairwise rates do not establish that every zero-LN SGD net is frozen, nor that one LN removes all attenuation.
